ci_method: Exact Clopper-Pearson binomial 95% interval on declining wells among determinate wells, treating wells as independent units
independent_unit: The well: one last-in-period result per well per period; repeated samples within a well and nearby wells (shared aquifer, lab, method changes) are not independent, so intervals are likely too narrow.
nondetect_sensitivity: Main method uses interval bounds (non-detect = [0, limit]); a pair is determinate only if intervals do not overlap. Substitution as sensitivity (labelled): zero -> 149 decline/108 increase/38 ties; half-limit -> 153/107/35; full-limit -> 152/108/35. Direction (more declines than increases) does not change; median late/early ratio 0.95-0.98. Only 31 cohort wells have a censored result in each period, so non-detects cannot drive the result. But limits vary 0.02-100 ug/L and rose in 2015-2018 (up to 100), and the early period has more censoring (11% vs 4% of results), which can mask or create apparent change for low-concentration wells.
notes: Filter: USGS 01000 dissolved As, ActivityTypeCode Sample-Routine, ActivityMediaSubdivisionName Groundwater (2997 of 3562 arsenic rows; excluded 162 field replicates, 34 undetermined, 1 reference material, 3 total-As 01002 rows, and elutriation/soil-moisture/interstitial/leachate rows). Units all ug/L, no conversion. 3 'Detected Not Quantified' rows treated as [0, reporting level]. Last result per well per period by date/time. Cohort 295 wells (659 early wells, 629 late wells; pooled comparison would mix different wells). 146 decline, 105 increase, 44 indeterminate. Share declining of all cohort wells = 0.495 (exact 95% CI 0.436-0.553); among determinate wells 0.582 (CI 0.518-0.643). Median ratio over 257 both-detected wells, well bootstrap 95% CI 0.929-1.000. Classification uses strict inequality of reported values with no analytic-error allowance, so small differences count as change. Methods changed over time (PLM10, PLM40/42, GF085, PLM62; some blank) and results are partly Preliminary.
